title: Preserve accepted VCF Installer bootstrap steps when sync fails
prompt:
Implement the unfinished `VcfInstallerClient.java` as a dependency-free Java 17 client for a three-step VMware Cloud Foundation Installer 9.1 bootstrap change. Keep the implementation in that single Java file, preserve its public API and nested types, and do not edit the harness, mock, contract, or provenance files.

The protected `docs/contract.json` is a focused projection derived directly from `specifications/vcf-installer/vcf-installer-openapi.json` in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository at immutable VCF 9.1 release-readiness commit `c3f3b52c845dd967cabbc21680e893292077d5ba`. `docs/official_sources.json` records that commit SHA, the exact specification path, and a separate specification source record for every operationId. No rendered documentation page is a contract source. Call exactly `updateProxyConfiguration`, `updateDepotSettings`, and `syncDepotMetadata`, in that order; do not call any other route.

Preserve `new VcfInstallerClient(String baseUrl, String accessToken)`, `ChangeReport configureDepotAccess(ProxyConfiguration proxy, DepotSettings depot)`, every supplied request record, `Outcome`, `StepStatus`, `StepResult`, `ChangeReport`, and the exception hierarchy. The service root must be an absolute HTTP or HTTPS URL with a host and no userinfo, non-root path, query, or fragment. Reject a blank or header-unsafe token. Reject null top-level workflow arguments before sending anything. Never expose the access token, proxy password, depot password, or download credentials in an exception message.

The workflow stops after its first failure and never rolls back, replays, or skips an earlier accepted call. Treat only exact HTTP 202 as accepted; 202 means `ACCEPTED`, not completed server-side work. Every report contains exactly three ordered results for the three operationIds. Start unattempted steps as `NOT_RUN`. An accepted step records `ACCEPTED` and 202; the proxy result additionally records the task ID from its accepted response. A failed attempted step records `FAILED`, its actual status when a response exists, and decoded VCF `errorCode` and `message` when present. Use HTTP status 0 for a step for which no response exists, including every `NOT_RUN` step. Use outcome `ACCEPTED` only when all three requests are accepted, `FAILED` when the first step fails, and `PARTIAL_FAILURE` when a later step fails after at least one acceptance. Every `ChangeException` must carry that immutable snapshot in `report()`.

For non-202 responses throw `VcfApiException`, preserving its operationId, HTTP status, and the focused VCF Error fields `errorCode`, `errorType`, `message`, `remediationMessage`, and `referenceToken`. A request failure throws a secret-safe `TransportException`. A malformed accepted response throws `ProtocolException`. All accepted responses require a JSON media type and a JSON object. The proxy response must contain nonblank specification-required Task members `id`, `name`, `status`, and `creationTimestamp`; the sync response must contain a nonblank specification-required `syncStatus`. If an HTTP call is interrupted, restore the thread's interrupted status before failing the current step.

Honor the exact wire contract. Every request has exactly one `Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>` and one `Accept: application/json`, with no query or bare `?`. `updateProxyConfiguration` is `PATCH /v1/system/proxy-configuration`; `updateDepotSettings` is `PUT /v1/system/settings/depot`. Each has one compact UTF-8 JSON object, exactly one `Content-Type: application/json`, a fixed content length, and no transfer encoding. `syncDepotMetadata` is a bodyless `PATCH /v1/system/settings/depot/depot-sync-info` with no `Content-Type`, transfer encoding, or positive content length.

Serialize members in the supplied record declaration order. Null request components are unset and must be omitted at every nesting level, never sent as JSON null, an empty placeholder object, an empty string, zero, or false. Non-null values are explicit, so preserve empty strings, numeric zero, and false. When a `DepotConfiguration` object is present its primitive `isOfflineDepot` is required and is always emitted. Never send the read-only proxy `isConfigured`, synthesize depot account `status` or `message`, or send Task or DepotSyncInfo response members. Correctly JSON-escape runtime strings.

Run `java TestMain.java`. The protected verifier starts the shipped contract-pinned mock on ephemeral `127.0.0.1` ports and reads its synchronized request log. The main scenario accepts the proxy and depot settings requests, then returns the specification-declared HTTP 500 from depot sync. Verification asserts the exact request sequence, methods, raw targets, header multiplicity, body bytes, content lengths, error preservation, accurate accepted/failed/not-run reports at each failure position, explicit empty/zero/false preservation, and omission of every unset optional field. The mock loads and serves only the three operations named by `docs/contract.json`. No live VMware endpoint is contacted.
scenario: updateProxyConfiguration and updateDepotSettings are accepted with HTTP 202, then syncDepotMetadata fails with HTTP 500; the thrown exception's report must retain both earlier acceptances and identify the failed final step.
constraint: The contract-pinned loopback request log proves exact compact JSON and nested optional-member omission while the immutable failure report proves precise partial progress.
